exposure: endoscopic intervention for idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) (laser wedge excision, balloon dilation)
cohort: Twelve pregnant patients with symptomatic idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) who underwent endoscopic intervention.
finding: Endoscopic intervention for idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) during pregnancy appears safe and effective, even in high-risk cases.
followup_time: Up to 11 months after delivery (for some patients undergoing additional procedures and for postpartum complications)
